justification: Changes the street frontage length shown on the page and used by the yield and eligibility checks, and which lot widths the Housing SEPP API accepts

falsifiable_check.command: pytest tests/test_street_frontage.py && cd frontend-nextjs && npx jest __tests__/lib/geometry/street-frontage.test.ts __tests__/lib/schemas/housing-sepp-width.test.ts
falsifiable_check.fails_when: the frontage differs from an external answer: the hand-measured street edges of real lots read off the NSW cadastre and road corridor maps on 2026-10-18 (Winston Hills 13.34 m, Padstow 15.27 m, Mortdale 6.19 m, Haberfield 26.25 m), or the known geometric answer of a synthetic lot (road beside 12 m of a 20 m edge = 12 m); or the API accepts half a width range or min above max. Not self-referential: the expected numbers come from the maps and geometry, not from this code.
falsifiable_check.observed_red: On origin/main a 20 m edge with the road beside its first 12 m reports frontage_m = 20 (edge counted whole once 50% qualifies); test_edge_only_partly_beside_the_road_counts_only_that_part fails there. HousingSEPPSchema on origin/main accepts {lotWidth:15, lotWidthMin:20, lotWidthMax:5} because the refine passes as soon as lotWidth is present.

pre_impl.existing_data: NSW road corridor layer parcels with roadnamelabel; lot boundary rings in EPSG:3857
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: a gap shorter than 3 m at either end of a road edge is counted as frontage (corner curves); the width profile still starts from the whole edge
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: every page and report that shows street frontage after deploy

falsifiable_check.fails_when: the frontage differs from an external answer: the hand-measured street edges of real lots read off the NSW cadastre and road corridor maps on 2026-10-18 (Winston Hills 13.34 m, Padstow 15.27 m, Mortdale 6.19 m, Haberfield 26.25 m), or the known geometric answer of a synthetic lot (road beside 12 m of a 20 m edge = 12 m); or the API accepts half a width range or min above max. Not self-referential: the expected numbers come from the maps and geometry, not from this code.

functions.name: measure_street_frontage
functions.input: the lot boundary ring and the road corridor parcels near it
functions.output: per named road: frontage length, front-half and widest width, depth
functions.if_none: no usable ring: unavailable; no road owns an edge: not_identified

functions.name: _edge_frontage_share
functions.input: one lot edge and the road segments of one road
functions.output: the share of the edge beside that road, with gaps up to 3 m ignored
functions.if_none: a zero-length edge contributes 0 m whatever its share

values.guard_at: refine: both or neither, min <= max
values.if_missing: lotWidth alone is accepted; neither is a 400

break_it.scenario: road beside only part of a lot edge
break_it.what_happens: frontage overstated by the uncovered part
break_it.how: only the share beside the road counts; gaps over 3 m cut

break_it.what_happens: road B could fill road A's gap
break_it.how: each road measured against its own parcels

break_it.scenario: a short real break in the middle of a road edge
break_it.what_happens: would be filled in as frontage although no road is beside it
break_it.how: only gaps at the two ends of an edge (corner curves) are filled; a middle gap is always cut

post_merge.manual_verify: Yes — Winston Hills still reads 13.3 m along Berrigan St; Haberfield 26.3 m along Logan Ave
